ground_truth.description: `_checkpoint` creates a new epoch with the same timestamp for `increase_amount`, ignoring the new lock in `balanceOfNFT`, reducing voting power.
ground_truth.root_cause: `_checkpoint` creates a new epoch with the same timestamp for `increase_amount`, ignoring the new lock in `balanceOfNFT`, reducing voting power.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: A test locks 500e18, increases by 500e18 in one tx, and shows reduced bribe rewards compared to separate locks.
ground_truth.fix_description: In `_checkpoint`, overwrite the latest point if timestamps match, else append a new one. Status: Mitigation confirmed.

vulnerabilities.explanation: When create_lock + increase_amount (or multiple deposits) occur in one tx, _checkpoint appends a new point_history entry with identical timestamp to the prior one instead of overwriting. balanceOfNFT uses the latest point by timestamp; duplicate ts causes it to read stale slope/bias, under-calculating voting power.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Alice calls create_lock(500e18, ...) then increase_amount(tokenId, 500e18) in same tx. 2. _deposit_for calls _checkpoint twice with same block.timestamp. 3. Second checkpoint writes point_history[epoch] at same ts. 4. balanceOfNFT reads the first (pre-increase) point, returning ~half expected votes. 5. Bribe/reward calculations using votes distribute less to Alice.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: In _checkpoint after computing last_point, if point_history[_epoch].ts == block.timestamp then overwrite it; else append and increment epoch.

prediction.overall_explanation: The documented logic error in _checkpoint produces incorrect (reduced) voting power when multiple lock operations share a timestamp. This directly affects downstream reward distribution without requiring any privileged role.
